newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Smurfit Fund invests five mln punts.
newsitem.headline: Smurfit Fund invests five mln punts.

text.p: Smurfit Job Creation Enterprise Fund invested five million Irish pounds and created 215 new jobs in targeted investment in small-to-medium sized Irish firms in the last three years, chairman Liam Connellan said on Tuesday.
The fund was established in 1993 by Irish paper and packaging company Jefferson Smurfit Group Plc with the aim of investing in growth-oriented Irish companies.
Since its foundation, it has made 23 investments in 19 companies, Connellan said in a statement.
Investment is spread in different parts of the country and includes a wide range of industries and services ranging from healthcare to software, engineering and equestrian clothing.

At least 39 percent of the fund's investment was in businesses established over five years and under 10 years, 24 percent in those established less than five years, 23 percent in mature companies and 14 percent in start-ups, the statement said.
Connellan said it was too early to assess the likely outcome in respect of the return the fund may have on its investments as its planned exit dates had not yet been reached.
But he added that the trading performance was satisfactory with annualised sales of 32 million Irish pounds.
Overall pre-tax profit was annualised at 1.9 million and capital employed totalled 15 million punts, he said.
Smurfit has also established a venutre capital company, Smurfit Venture Investments, which has 10 million Irish pounds available for growth-oriented Irish business.
The money is being jointly provided by the Jefferson Smurfit Group and Irish industrial development agency Forbairt using European Union Structural Funds.

The investment range will be a minimum of 100,000 Irish pounds and a maximum of 500,000 Irish pounds and each successful applicant will be expected to create at least 10 new jobs over a three-year period after investment.
